text:
maya-support: SoraHealth reporting repeated 429s during their nightly sync (23:59-00:03 UTC). They say the sync spins up ~120 containers at once and sends ~1.8k short POSTs in 40s.

sora-ops: yes, we're seeing lots of 429s in prod. plan is "professional" (400 rpm). sample response attached.

maya-support: pasted one 429 header/body from their logs below.

maya-support: ```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-limit: 400
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 1715554500
retry-after: 12
content-type: application/json
{ \"error\": \"rate_limited\", \"message\": \"rpm exceeded\" }
```

devin-eng: that looks like per-minute RPM exhaustion (limit 400). burst is concentrated around the minute boundary so binning kills the remaining window.

lina-sre: quick triage checklist: check request timestamps binned to minute buckets, look for high fanout (many clients) vs single client multi-stream http/2, verify whether requests are identical (could use prefix caching).

sora-ops: our job uses Kubernetes CronJobs — all pods start at 23:59 exactly. we didn't add jitter.

devin-eng: there's the smoking gun. Two immediate mitigation paths: client-side smoothing or a temporary quota increase while they refactor. Client jitter + backoff is best long-term.

maya-support: asked them to run a repro with timestamps and a sample curl to capture headers. suggested this command:

maya-support: ```bash
curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>\" -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"test"}'
```

lina-sre: also asked infra to run a log query for their tenant sora-prod-7 around 1715554440-1715554540. internal query we use:

lina-sre: ```text
service=api edge tenant_id=sora-prod-7 | where status==429 | bin by minute | count() | sort desc
```

infra-bot: alert: tenant=sora-prod-7 429-rate spike at 1715554489, created incident INC-2026-519.

devin-eng: recommended mitigation options to SoraHealth:
- add jitter (random 0-60s) to cronjob start times and ensure pods stagger their requests
- implement exponential backoff with full jitter on 429 responses
- consider a small ramp/worker-leasing approach to keep concurrent requests under plan limits
- if immediate business need, request a short-term soft RPM bump while they roll out fixes

sora-ops: we'd like a temporary increase to 2k rpm for 3 days while we patch jobs. can you confirm impact?

maya-support: filed an internal request for a soft bump: ticket INC-2026-519. asked SRE to approve a 2k rpm soft increase for 72h and to monitor cost/TPM impact.

lina-sre: approved provisional bump for 72h, will revert unless we see upgrade or smoothing rollout. set watch: rpm > 1500 for 5m => pager.

devin-eng: couple of engineering checks to run while bump is active:
- confirm rate window semantics for this tenant (UTC minute buckets vs sliding window)
- check whether any AZ skew or sticky routing concentrated their traffic on a small set of ratecarriers
- enable prefix caching if many requests share the same prompt prefix to cut TPM usage

sora-ops: we'll roll jitter out tonight to staging and replay a scaled copy of the job, then deploy to prod after validating headers.

maya-support: please post results here after staging replay. created a dashboard tile for sora-prod-7 showing rpm, 429 count and top endpoints.

infra-bot: monitor rule created: sora-prod-7 rpm > 1500 (5m) => warn, INC-2026-519 updated.

maya-support: closing loop for now  customer accepted plan: temporary bump + job smoothing. we'll run a follow-up check after 72h and schedule a brief postmortem if pattern repeats.

sora-ops: thanks all, deploying jitter now.

maya-support: note for runbook: prefer client jitter + backoff, avoid granting permanent rpm increases unless tenant upgrades plan or moves to Dedicated.
